subject: CycloSync: performance signoff plan and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Alex Nolan <alex.nolan@cyclosync.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: support@cyclosync.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: onboarding checklist - performance targets

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are starting the integration and need to lock acceptance targets so our SREs can run their load passes next week. Can you confirm what you need from us for a final signoff? Specifically:
- Target P95 latency under sustained load (100k tokens/min)
- Peak qps and concurrency to simulate
- Any specific test payloads or prompt sets to use

We have a hard launch goal for the first week of January, so the sooner we agree the better. I can attach sample requests if that helps.

Best,
Alex
Director of Engineering
CycloSync
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Alex Nolan <alex.nolan@cyclosync.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: CycloSync: performance signoff plan and acceptance criteria

Alex,

Thanks — great to see the timeline. Attached is a concise signoff plan that we use for Dedicated onboarding (performance-signoff-plan-cyclosync-v1.pdf). Key items in short:

1) Goals we expect from your SRE verification
- P95 inference latency <= 220 ms for text-generation baseline at 1k token average prompt, under steady-state 80% of peak traffic.
- Sustained throughput equivalent to 100k tokens/min (approx 55 QPS on our baseline model with 512-token avg output).
- Peak burst capacity validated at 200 QPS for 5-minute windows without error-rate increase > 1%.

2) What we need from CycloSync
- A representative prompt set (1000 prompts) and a 60-minute traffic trace (or synthetic generator)
- Preferred test window(s) and IP allowlist for our test runners
- Any on-prem or VPC network constraints noted up front

3) Our test plan highlights
- Three passes: warmup, sustained 60-minute pass at declared peak, burst test, plus a recovery assessment.
- We will run KV-cache warmed and cold runs for comparison.
- We will capture token-level timing, error rates, and tail-latency histograms and share csv artifacts.

If those numbers look reasonable, confirm the peak qps CycloSync will target so Connor and I can schedule a dedicated run. I propose Wed Nov 24 03:00-05:00 UTC for the sustained pass (we can shift).

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, Alex Nolan <alex.nolan@cyclosync.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T12:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CycloSync: performance signoff plan and acceptance criteria

Alex/Vanessa,

Quick technical notes from the runtime team before we lock windows:
- For the sustained 100k tokens/min target we estimate ~52 QPS if average prompt+response is ~115 tokens. Please confirm your expected average tokens per request (input+output).
- Network: please allow 52.23.10.0/24 and 52.23.11.0/24 for test runners; ephemeral ports 49152-65535 outbound.
- We will enable prefix caching on run 2 to show improvement; please flag any stateful prompt templates that would invalidate caching.
- We'll produce two artifact types: timing_histogram.csv and per_request_samples.jsonl. The csv will be the primary acceptance artifact.

If you lock the average tokens and confirm an exact peak QPS candidate we will reserve a slot and spin up the test harness.

Connor O
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Nolan <alex.nolan@cyclosync.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: support@cyclosync.com
Date: 2026-11-22T07:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CycloSync: performance signoff plan and acceptance criteria

Connor, Vanessa,

Thanks for the clarity. Our SREs ran an internal pass and propose these numbers:
- Average tokens per request (input+output): 130
- Sustained target: 100k tokens/min -> roughly 77 QPS at 130 tokens/request
- Peak burst target: 220 QPS for 5 minutes

We can provide the 1k prompt set and a 60-minute synthetic generator (will attach sample payloads). We can also run the warmup pass on Tue Nov 24 03:00-04:00 UTC and the sustained pass Wed Nov 25 03:00-04:00 UTC. Would Redwood prefer both on the same day?

Attaching: cyc_sample_requests_v1.json (sample payloads). We'll upload full results after our local run and share the CSV.

Alex
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Nolan <alex.nolan@cyclosync.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CycloSync: performance signoff plan and acceptance criteria

Alex — thanks, this works. Confirming the agreed plan and next steps:

- Targets locked: P95 <= 220 ms (as measured by Redwood test harness), sustained 77 QPS (100k tokens/min at 130 tokens/req), peak burst 220 QPS.
- Warmup: Tue Nov 24 03:00-04:00 UTC (Redwood will observe, no pass/fail yet).
- Sustained acceptance pass: Wed Nov 25 03:00-04:00 UTC. Redwood to produce timing_histogram.csv and per_request_samples.jsonl within 4 hours of completion.
- CycloSync to share the 1k prompt set and the synthetic generator; drop in the Drive folder linked above.

After the sustained pass we will review artifacts together and either sign the performance acceptance or outline remediation items. If acceptance criteria pass, Marissa on CS will schedule the production cutover checklist.

I have uploaded a short signoff plan and added the test artifacts folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPerfSignoff_CycloSync

Thanks everyone — see you on the 24th for warmup.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
